# Inside the Tártaros restoration: what the marks recover
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Tártaros** is what the evidence put back.

Tártaros appears almost as soon as the world begins. It is the third primordial in Hesiod's list — gap, earth, abyss — and it remains the final destination for every cosmic rebel. After Cháos and Gaia, Hesiod names Tártaros: "dim Tartarus, in the depths of the broad-pathed earth" (Theogony 119).  It is both a place and a power, the body of the pit itself.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Tártaros
- **ASCII form:** tartaros
- **Meaning:** "Deep place (from τάρταρος)"
- **Domain of influence:** The Primordial Abyss
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** Τάρταρος
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 235 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Τάρταρος**. On the evidence, it means "Deep place (from τάρταρος)".

Strip **Tártaros** to *tartaros* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → á** — Acute on alpha: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

None of these marks is decoration. Each one is a fact about how the name was spoken, and each one is checkable against the scholarly record the temple cites.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Tártaros** lives at [/sites/tartaros/](/sites/tartaros/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/tartaros/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/tartaros/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/tartaros/patterns/).

The restoration preserves one decisive feature the ASCII form drops — a single, honest mark — which places it in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Tártaros** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP** — Persona 3’s Tartarus towered over a generation of players.
- **Defense, Military & Security** — The prison that held the Titans; the logic of containment.
- **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** — Second Peter casts the sinning angels into Tartarus; the abyss entered Christian scripture.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/tartaros/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
